catalogue_requests.reason: Return the instrument identity string of the *IDN? query through the identify tool.
Read the oscilloscope status object the get_status tool returns (trigger status, acquisition, timebase, channels); no catalogue class has this output.
Start, stop, arm, autoset, clear or force-trigger oscilloscope acquisition; the catalogue has no acquisition run-control class.
Change several analog-channel settings in one tool call and return the queried settings; cap.device.configure.v1 writes resource parameters, not this tool contract.
Set main timebase scale and offset through one tool call with its queried readback.
Configure edge triggering (mode EDGE, source, slope, level, sweep) with queried readback.
Set memory depth, acquisition type and average count with queried readback and sample rate.
Set the cursor mode, type and sources of an oscilloscope.
Manual TIME cursors with coordinates in seconds; a typed projection of the configure_cursors tool.
Manual AMPLitude cursors with coordinates in volts; a typed projection of the configure_cursors tool.
Manual cursors on the retained cursor type; a source-cited selection over the configure_cursors tool.
Read cursor positions and deltas in one of three mode-dependent shapes, published as a JSON artifact.
Select and read one of 33 automatic oscilloscope measurement items on one channel; cap.measure.voltage.v1 covers voltage only and has a different output.
Select and read a delay or phase item between two channels.
Capture a screen or deep-memory waveform with statistics and the decimated time/voltage arrays as a JSON artifact; the catalogue has no waveform acquisition class.
Capture the oscilloscope display as a PNG image artifact; cap.sensing.image.v1 is a camera image class.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored (claude-opus-5-5, a model, as the McpClientDriver family exemplar); reviewed_by stays null and no human review, hardware run or real MCP server run is claimed. SCOPE: all thirteen default tools of rigol_dho_mcp/server.py at f9ac7191 (server.py:147-600) as sixteen bindings; configure_cursors has three extra typed bindings so cursor coordinates carry seconds or volts. NOT COVERED: the opt-in scpi_command raw SCPI tool (registered only when RIGOL_ENABLE_SCPI_RAW is true, server.py:62,608-628) and the rigol-dho-cli command line (rigol_dho_mcp/cli.py). RISK: R0, checked against the 04-safety.md section 2.1 table (R0: data only, no physical effect; R1 starts at low-energy reversible physical actions such as small motion, illumination or a valve). The tools do write instrument state (run_control, the configure_* tools, and the select-then-query measurements), and R0 does not imply read-only (same section). Every exposed write sets how the scope acquires, triggers, displays or measures its own inputs: channel display, scale, offset, coupling, probe ratio, bandwidth limit and inversion (server.py:243-256), timebase (:275-279), edge trigger (:296-304), acquisition depth, type and averages (:323-328), cursors (:371-390), measurement selection (:454, 493) and run, stop, single, autoset, clear and force-trigger (:211-219). None sources a signal, current or voltage, moves anything or dispenses: no output or generator command is exposed, and the raw SCPI tool that could reach one is off by default and not bound. The worst consequences are a wrong configuration, recoverable by reconfiguring, and loss of an unsaved on-screen acquisition (clear, run, single, autoset), which is data loss, not a physical effect. R0 is kept; a reviewer who wants write-capable tools at R1 can raise it, and the protective run_control stop already exists. SAFE STATE: the e-stop sends run_control stop on the protective lane and requires a fresh get_status trigger_status of STOP after all older requests retired; that is proven for the controlled peer only. A real DHO's reaction to :STOP was not run. NATIVE: McpClientDriver and native.py refuse every non-fake backend before import, process start or connection (G7 warning MCP_NATIVE_UNRESOLVED, expected). The fake speaks the SDK's controlled MCP profile. Per the SDK's reviewed source assessment (MHS/sdk/docs/mcp-client.md, native compatibility section), the pinned FastMCP server (requirements.lock: mcp==1.29.0) lists pydantic-generated input schemas that differ from the declared closed schemas and can return structuredContent beside string results (identify and run_control return str); the bridge refuses both, so the package cannot drive the real server as it is. Server-process ownership (stdio or streamable-http), whole-tool retirement (each tool issues several SCPI calls, scpi.py:156-174) and exclusive instrument ownership remain unresolved. FAKE DATA: every number in fake.py is a placeholder. The fake returns a 1031-sample screen and a 20001-sample memory record and a 3 x 2 PNG; a real screen read is about 1000 points (server.py:515), deep memory can be up to 50M points (memory_depth enum, server.py:135) before the server decimates it to about max_points (server.py:576-582), and a real screenshot is a full-display PNG. The JSON waveform bound is 1 MiB and the PNG bound 1 MiB (2097152 pixels); a larger real result is refused, not truncated. TIMING: request_timeout_ms 500, stop_timeout_ms 500 and max_duration_ms 1000 (get_waveform, get_screenshot) are placeholder budgets of the controlled peer (driver.py CONTROLLED_* constants), not Rigol timings: the pinned server waits up to 30 s per deep-memory chunk, 15 s per screen read and 20 s for a screenshot (server.py:544,547,599), its socket timeout defaults to 10 s (server.py:61), and one tool issues several SCPI calls, so a real server could not meet them. They cannot go into fidelity gaps: a hardware-mode McpClientDriver served on its fake backend gets the SDK's fixed fake fidelity (F0, gap 'transport replaced by fake backend', mhs/driver/build.py:73-83,176-185) and has no fidelity declaration. LIMITS: channel indices 1-4 and max_points 10-10000 cite the tool signatures (server.py:230,443,478,479,512,517); the 1-4 range is the same for every model, and the source does not say how a model with fewer analog channels answers a channel it lacks (not verified); every other number (scale, offset, probe ratio, trigger level, average count, cursor coordinates) is Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a Rigol range. DECISION_DEVIATION (collect.py note): this card was generated while triage.py still had Family('mcp-client', None, 'helper:mcp-client', None), so it says family-config with helper null and blocked_on helper:mcp-client. The driver derives from McpClientDriver, the helper of the card's own family; it is not a deviation from the card's decision or family. The triage change that names McpClientDriver and this exemplar, followed by the registry rebuild and prepare.py --sync, sets the card's helper to McpClientDriver and the note disappears; no override is needed. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-sonnet-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Different-model review of a package authored by claude-opus-5-5 (the user chose Claude Sonnet as the different model, 2026-11-04): Gate and collect --strict re-run clean (digest unchanged); the unsourced timing numbers are now named placeholders with the real server timeouts cited correctly, the DECISION_DEVIATION is explained in the notes, and R0 is reasoned against the hazard table in facts.md. It uses McpClientDriver honestly: fake-only, native refuses, no stop effect on a real scope claimed. The owner may still choose R1. For the human reviewer: owner may prefer R1 (nit); collect.py DECISION_DEVIATION note persists until the registry rebuild
